```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Staging demo: needs the in-tree build (ATLS, #566; builds on PM, #523). Resolve
# the package root whether rendered from the repo root or from
# overstorey_staging/. Set ATLS_DEMO_PLANT=installed to render against the
# installed plant instead of a pkgload::load_all() build, which compiles without
# optimisation and makes the SCM sections far slower.
pkg_root <- if (file.exists("DESCRIPTION")) "." else ".."
if (identical(Sys.getenv("ATLS_DEMO_PLANT"), "installed") ||
    !requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  library(plant)
} else {
  pkgload::load_all(pkg_root, quiet = TRUE)
}
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Shared driving code (also exercised by tests/testthat/test-atls-leaf-demo.R,
# so this demo cannot silently rot).
source(file.path(pkg_root, "overstorey_staging", "atls_demo_helpers.R"))

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 12))
# One colour per strategy archetype, reused across the document.
strat_pal <- c("Generalist" = "#7570b3", "Tolerant" = "#d95f02",
               "Repairer" = "#1b9e77", "Acclimated" = "#e7298a")

# File-based cache for the expensive SCM runs: computed once, reused on
# re-render. Keyed on the cache name AND the deparsed call, so editing a chunk's
# call invalidates that entry. A rebuilt model is NOT tracked: delete
# overstorey_staging/cache/ to force a rerun after changing the model.
cache_dir <- file.path(pkg_root, "overstorey_staging", "cache")
dir.create(cache_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
cached_rds <- function(name, expr) {
  call_txt <- paste(deparse(substitute(expr)), collapse = " ")
  path <- file.path(cache_dir, paste0(name, ".rds"))
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    hit <- readRDS(path)
    if (identical(hit$call, call_txt)) return(hit$value)
  }
  value <- expr
  saveRDS(list(call = call_txt, value = value), path)
  value
}
```

The **ATLS** layer (leaf thermal damage, repair and acclimation, issue #566) gives a TF24 leaf a lasting response to heat on top of the reversible peaked-Arrhenius capacity curve. The leaf area is split into three fractions: **functional** `F`, **impaired** `I` and **damaged** `D`, with `F = 1 − I − D`. Functional leaf is impaired at a rate `k_imp(T)` that a smooth **switch** turns on around its midpoint `impair_Tmid` (34.5 °C at the defaults, its own parameter, independent of the Jmax curve). Impaired leaf is repaired back to functional over about 4 days, or matures into damaged leaf, which clears only as the plant grows new leaf. Both capacities scale by `F`, so a cooled leaf does *not* rebound instantly.

The layer and its dynamics live in phylloptim's `Leaf` behind `use_thermal_damage_`; the `TF24t` strategy turns it on, integrates the states on the plant, and dilutes damaged leaf with new growth. The equations are in `TF24t_leaf_ATLS_model.qmd`.

A thermal *strategy* is a point in a four-axis trait space, all plugging into the same physics:

| Axis | Knob | Moves |
|---|---|---|
| **Tolerance** (constitutive) | `topt_offset` | shifts the capacity optimum *and* the impairment switch up together |
| **Acclimation** (inducible) | `A` state | the same shift, induced when the regime is hot |
| **Repair** | preventive `k_i`, restorative `k_rec` | impair more slowly or repair faster (and cut the lasting floor) |
| **Avoidance** | transpirational cooling (energy balance) | lowers the operating leaf temperature, hence `k_imp` |

This demo drives a single well-watered leaf, then a single-species stand. It is a work-in-progress staging document, not a built vignette. See `notes/atls/implementation-plan.md` for the design and `notes/plan-atls-port.md` for the port to phylloptim.

## 1. The impairment rate `k_imp(Tleaf)` and the impairment it drives

The generalist (default) leaf: the impairment rate sits near 0 when cold, passes through **half of `k_i` at the switch midpoint ≈ 34.5 °C** (`impair_Tmid`, marked), and saturates toward `k_i` when hot. Leaf temperature is *prescribed* here, so this is the pure mechanism with no optimiser in the loop.

The right-hand panel shows the standing impaired fraction this rate would drive, `I* = k_imp / (k_imp + k_rec_eff + k_mat)` (with `D = 0`): the balance the `I` ODE relaxes toward at a held temperature. A fresh leaf loses no capacity instantly; impairment is a *memory* that fills over days, and each unit of `I` or `D` removes that share of **both** `vcmax` and `jmax`.

```{r damage-curve}
Tleaf <- seq(20, 50, by = 0.5)
kimp_gen <- atls_k_imp_curve(Tleaf, atls_traits())
I_gen    <- atls_I_star_curve(Tleaf, atls_traits())
onset <- atls_traits()$impair_Tmid   # about 34.5 deg C

p_kimp <- ggplot(data.frame(Tleaf, k = kimp_gen), aes(Tleaf, k)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#d95f02", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = onset, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = onset + 0.4, y = 0.02, label = "impair_Tmid", hjust = 0,
           size = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  labs(x = "leaf temperature (°C)", y = "k_imp (day⁻¹)",
       title = "Impairment rate k_imp(Tleaf)")

p_I <- ggplot(data.frame(Tleaf, I = I_gen), aes(Tleaf, I)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#7570b3", linewidth = 0.9) +
  ylim(0, 1) +
  labs(x = "leaf temperature (°C)", y = "I* (quasi-steady)",
       title = "Standing impaired fraction")

p_kimp | p_I
```

## 2. Four thermal-response strategies move the impairment differently

Each archetype is a single-axis move off the generalist, shown as the standing impaired fraction `I*(Tleaf)`. **Tolerance** and **acclimation** shift the switch (and hence `I*`) to higher temperature; **repair** (higher `k_rec`, lower `k_i`) lowers `I*` at a given temperature. Avoidance is not a curve shift — it lowers the *operating* temperature, shown in §4.

```{r strategy-curves}
strategies <- atls_strategies()
I_curves <- bind_rows(lapply(names(strategies), function(nm) {
  data.frame(strategy = nm, Tleaf = Tleaf,
             I = atls_I_star_curve(Tleaf, strategies[[nm]]))
}))

ggplot(I_curves, aes(Tleaf, I, colour = strategy)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = strat_pal, name = NULL) +
  ylim(0, 1) +
  labs(x = "leaf temperature (°C)", y = "I* (quasi-steady impaired fraction)",
       title = "Standing impairment I*(Tleaf) by thermal strategy",
       subtitle = "Tolerant/Acclimated shift the switch right; Repairer lowers the whole curve") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 3. Who keeps carbon where? Assimilation across a heat gradient

The payoff, on fresh leaves (`I = D = 0`, so the assimilation panel isolates the reversible-capacity effect). Tolerance and acclimation raise the capacity optimum (`topt_offset`, `A`), buying carbon at hot leaf temperatures; the standing-impairment panel shows where impairment *would* accrue over days.

```{r strategy-assim}
grad <- atls_solve_strategies(seq(24, 48, by = 2), strategies,
                              PAR = 1500, VPD = 2)

p_grad_A <- ggplot(grad, aes(Tenv, A, colour = strategy)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = strat_pal, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "leaf temperature (°C)", y = "assimilation (µmol C m⁻² s⁻¹)",
       title = "Carbon gain by strategy")

p_grad_I <- ggplot(grad, aes(Tenv, I_star, colour = strategy)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = strat_pal, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "leaf temperature (°C)", y = "I* at the operating point",
       title = "Standing impairment by strategy")

(p_grad_I | p_grad_A) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 4. Avoidance: transpirational cooling as the fourth axis

Avoidance is not a damage trait — it is the leaf keeping itself cooler than it would otherwise be by transpiring, through the Penman–Monteith energy balance (#523). A better-coupled leaf (smaller dimension `d`, higher conductance) runs closer to air temperature, so on a hot day it is impaired more slowly and carries less lasting damage. Both leaves here are the generalist; only the coupling differs.

```{r avoidance}
avoid_cfgs <- list(
  "poorly coupled (large leaf, low g)" =
    atls_leaf_config(d = 0.10, leaf_specific_conductance_max = 2e-4),
  "well coupled (small leaf, high g)" =
    atls_leaf_config(d = 0.02, leaf_specific_conductance_max = 1e-3))

avoid <- bind_rows(lapply(names(avoid_cfgs), function(nm) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq(24, 40, by = 0.5), function(Tair) {
    r <- atls_solve_cell(1500, Tair, 2, atls_traits(), pm = TRUE,
                         cfg = avoid_cfgs[[nm]])
    data.frame(coupling = nm, Tair = Tair, Tleaf = r$Tleaf,
               k_imp = r$k_imp, A = r$A)
  }))
}))

avoid_pal <- c("poorly coupled (large leaf, low g)" = "#b2182b",
               "well coupled (small leaf, high g)" = "#2166ac")

p_av_T <- ggplot(avoid, aes(Tair, Tleaf, colour = coupling)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = avoid_pal, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "air temperature (°C)", y = "operating leaf temperature (°C)",
       title = "Cooling by coupling", subtitle = "dotted = Tleaf = Tair")

p_av_k <- ggplot(avoid, aes(Tair, k_imp, colour = coupling)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = avoid_pal, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "air temperature (°C)", y = "k_imp at the operating point (day⁻¹)",
       title = "... lowers the impairment rate")

(p_av_T | p_av_k) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

> An isolated, poorly coupled leaf under high radiation runs far above the air — more than 20 °C above it across this sweep — so the *absolute* temperatures here are an upper bound; the **contrast** between couplings is the robust signal.

## 5. From one leaf to a community: persistence under warming (SCM)

Everything above is a single isolated leaf. The demographic question is whether the damage feedback changes whether a *population* persists. We run the size-structured community model (SCM) — a single-species patch under a constant climate, with the `leaf_temp` driver as the midday air temperature — across a warming gradient, TF24t against TF24 with the energy balance on.

**How we measure fitness matters.** The net reproduction ratio R0 at a *fixed* seed rain is **not** a valid cross-strategy comparison: it conflates per-capita productivity with density-dependent recruitment. A less fecund resident shades the patch less, so at a shared seed rain each of its seeds does *better*, inflating its R0 although it is the weaker plant.

The density-free measure is **viability**: when *rare*, does a resident more than replace itself? R0 is evaluated in the low-density limit (a small `birth_rate`). R0 ≥ 1 means the population grows from rare and persists. The warmest climate with R0 ≥ 1 is the **persistence boundary**, and *that* is comparable across strategies, because density effects vanish as density goes to zero. We read the boundary, never the R0 magnitude away from it.

Each SCM run takes one to two minutes; the grid is cached to an `.rds` under `overstorey_staging/cache/` (delete that folder to force a rerun) and the runs are spread across cores.

```{r scm-viability}
# k_mat is a CALIBRATION TARGET. At its default (0.02/day) the permanent pool
# ratchets -- maturation influx DAYS_PER_YEAR*k_mat ~ 7.3/yr against the only
# sink, leaf turnover k_l ~ 0.46/yr -- which makes TF24t inviable in every
# climate. This section uses the balanced k_l/DAYS_PER_YEAR ~ 0.00125/day, the
# value the July runs used, so it is illustrative.
atls_scm_kmat <- 0.00125

scen5 <- list(
  "PM only (TF24)"    = list(type = "TF24"),
  "PM + ATLS (TF24t)" = list(type = "TF24t",
                             mutate = function(s) { s$k_mat <- atls_scm_kmat; s }))
# The cache name carries k_mat: the scenario list (hence k_mat) hides behind the
# `scen5` symbol, so the call text alone would not see a change to it.
viab5  <- cached_rds(sprintf("scm-viability-k%.5g", atls_scm_kmat),
                     atls_scm_viability(seq(23, 31, by = 1), scen5))
bound5 <- atls_persistence_boundary(viab5)
knitr::kable(bound5, digits = 1, col.names = c("scenario", "persistence °C"))

ggplot(viab5, aes(air_temp, pmax(log10(R0), -8), colour = scenario)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_vline(data = bound5, aes(xintercept = boundary, colour = scenario),
             linetype = "dotted", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 23, y = 0.35, label = "persistence (R0 = 1)",
           hjust = 0, size = 3, colour = "grey40") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("PM only (TF24)"    = "#1b9e77",
                                 "PM + ATLS (TF24t)" = "#d95f02"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "midday climate temperature (°C)",
       y = expression(log[10] * " R0 (low density)"),
       title = "Persistence boundary: warmest climate a rare population survives",
       subtitle = "low-density R0; the R0 = 1 crossing (dotted) is the density-free boundary") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The valid signal is the **persistence boundary** — the dotted crossings, not the curve heights, which still carry the density artifact and are drawn on a log scale only to expose the crossing.

> **Reading these results.** On the July code, ATLS moved the persistence boundary *cooler* than the energy balance alone: adding lasting thermal damage was a net persistence penalty (`notes/atls/results-2026-07/`). That reading has not been re-derived on the ported code, and on current code it cannot be read off this figure: with the energy balance on, this stand is far below replacement at every temperature in the range, with or without the thermal layer (TF24 with the balance on gives low-density R0 of 1e-8 at 15 °C and 1e-18 at 28 °C, against 56 at 25 °C with it off). No scenario crosses R0 = 1, so the table reports no boundary. The comparison needs re-setting — the baseline understood, or the climate range or traits moved — before it says anything about the thermal layer.

## 6. Which thermal strategy persists hottest? (SCM tournament)

Same measure, now varying the *strategy* — each a heritable single-axis move off the generalist (tolerance = constitutive `topt_offset`; repair = higher restorative `k_rec` and lower preventive `k_i`; acclimator = faster acclimation kinetics). "Persists hottest" means the highest **persistence boundary**, not the R0 height at a shared seed rain.

```{r scm-tournament}
# Each strategy carries the balanced k_mat from section 5, so the ranking is not
# swamped by the default permanent-damage ratchet.
scm_strats <- atls_scm_strategies()
scen6 <- setNames(lapply(names(scm_strats), function(nm) {
  base <- scm_strats[[nm]]
  list(type = "TF24t",
       mutate = function(s) { s <- base(s); s$k_mat <- atls_scm_kmat; s })
}), names(scm_strats))

viab6  <- cached_rds(sprintf("scm-viability-strat-k%.5g", atls_scm_kmat),
                     atls_scm_viability(seq(23, 33, by = 1), scen6))
bound6 <- atls_persistence_boundary(viab6)
bound6 <- bound6[order(-bound6$boundary), ]
knitr::kable(bound6, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("strategy", "persistence °C"))

strat_pal6 <- c("Generalist" = "#7570b3", "Tolerant" = "#d95f02",
                "Repairer" = "#1b9e77", "Acclimator" = "#e7298a")
ggplot(bound6, aes(reorder(scenario, boundary), boundary, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f °C", boundary)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = strat_pal6, guide = "none") +
  expand_limits(y = max(bound6$boundary, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.5) +
  labs(x = NULL,
       y = "persistence boundary (warmest climate with R0 ≥ 1, °C)",
       title = "Which thermal strategy persists hottest?",
       subtitle = "warmest climate at which a rare TF24t resident still replaces itself") +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))
```

> **Reading these results.** On the July code the order was **tolerance > repair > acclimation > generalist**, and tolerance and repair persisted hotter although their low-density R0 at cool climates was *lower* than the generalist's — the inversion that is why the ranking is by the R0 = 1 crossing. As in §5, that reading is July's and has not yet been re-derived on the ported code.

## 7. Memory: the running-mean leaf temperature

The sections above read the *instantaneous* operating leaf temperature. TF24t also carries a diagnostic ODE state, **`mean_leaf_temp`**, an exponential moving average of the operating-point `Tleaf`:

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}\,\overline{T_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t}
  = D\,k_{\overline{T}}\,\bigl(T_\ell - \overline{T_\ell}\bigr),
$$

where `T_ℓ` is the operating-point leaf temperature (TF24's `Tleaf` aux), `k_mean_leaf_temp` is the memory decay rate (day⁻¹; `D = 365.25` puts it on the yearly clock), and the memory is `1/k_mean_leaf_temp`. It is **purely diagnostic** — nothing reads it — so it is a clean read-out of the temperature history a plant has experienced. Below, a single TF24t individual is driven with an oscillating air temperature; the running mean lags and smooths the operating temperature (memory about 20 d here).

```{r running-mean, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
traj_wide <- cached_rds("running-mean", {
  e <- "TF24_Env"
  k_mem  <- 0.05               # day^-1, about a 20-day memory
  period <- 0.12               # yr (about 44 d), comparable to the memory
  t_end  <- 0.6                # yr

  s <- TF24t_Strategy(); s$k_mean_leaf_temp <- k_mem
  p <- Individual("TF24t", e)(s)
  env <- Environment("TF24t")
  # The adaptive stepper can probe the driver just past t_end, so the driver is
  # set on a grid beyond the loop horizon; outside its range the spline would
  # extrapolate.
  t_drive <- seq(0, t_end * 1.15, length.out = 230)
  env$extrinsic_drivers_set_variable("leaf_temp", t_drive,
                                     27 + 6 * sin(2 * pi * t_drive / period))
  # Seeded as a node would be: storage, A at equilibrium, and the running mean
  # at the birth air temperature.
  p$set_initial_states(env)

  runner <- plant:::OdeRunner("TF24t")(plant:::IndividualRunner("TF24t", e)(p, env))
  rec <- list()
  while (runner$time < t_end) {
    runner$step()
    ind <- runner$object$individual
    rec[[length(rec) + 1L]] <- data.frame(
      time      = runner$time,
      air_temp  = env$extrinsic_drivers_evaluate("leaf_temp", min(runner$time, t_end)),
      operating = ind$aux("Tleaf"),
      running   = ind$state("mean_leaf_temp"))
  }
  do.call(rbind, rec)
})
traj <- traj_wide |>
  pivot_longer(c(air_temp, operating, running), names_to = "series",
               values_to = "temp")

series_lab <- c(air_temp = "air temperature (driver)",
                operating = "operating leaf temp (instantaneous)",
                running = "mean_leaf_temp (running mean)")
series_pal <- c(air_temp = "grey60", operating = "#d95f02", running = "#1b9e77")

ggplot(traj, aes(time, temp, colour = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = series_pal, labels = series_lab, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "time (years)", y = "temperature (°C)",
       title = "mean_leaf_temp lags and smooths the operating leaf temperature",
       subtitle = "single TF24t individual, oscillating air temperature; memory about 20 d") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

The running mean (green) tracks the operating leaf temperature (orange) with a lag set by `k_mean_leaf_temp` and a reduced amplitude. The operating temperature sits above the air because a lone plant in full light runs hot (§4); its jumps and plateaus near the air-temperature peaks are the leaf shutting its stomata, after which nothing cools it. `mean_leaf_temp` averages that operating signal, not the driver.

## 8. Summary

The impairment rate `k_imp(Tleaf)` is the single driver: strategies act by moving *where its switch turns on* (tolerance and acclimation shift the midpoint), *how fast functional leaf is impaired and how fast it is repaired* (preventive `k_i`, restorative `k_rec`), or *where the leaf actually operates* (avoidance). Impairment is a **memory**: the impaired and damaged fractions remove their share of both capacities and persist after cooling, and damaged leaf clears only as the plant grows new leaf. At the community scale the same layer sets a **persistence boundary**, the warmest climate at which a rare population still replaces itself. Its value on the ported code, and the strategy ranking, are to be re-derived; both rest on open calibration items, among them the leaf overheating, the switch midpoint and the `k_mat` maturation rate. See `notes/atls/gate-atls-vs-pm-evaluation.md` for the July materiality gate.
